title: NIDCD says a deaf child of deaf signing parents acquires ASL as hearing children acquire speech
summary: NIDCD says a deaf child born to deaf parents who already use ASL begins to acquire it as naturally as a hearing child picks up spoken language.
body: The NIDCD ASL page says parents are often the source of a child's early language. A deaf child born to parents who are deaf and who already use ASL will begin to acquire ASL as naturally as a hearing child picks up spoken language from hearing parents. The comparison is the page's. It is about children who have that language around them from the start. It is not a claim about children whose families do not sign, which the page discusses separately. The page was updated in 2021.

sources.title: What Is American Sign Language?
sources.author: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.note: US federal page, public domain. Opened 2026-11-26. Last updated date printed on the page: 29 October 2021. Supports the sentence comparing ASL acquisition by a deaf child of deaf signing parents to spoken-language acquisition by a hearing child.
